title: Lane-shaping PRD for Hosted Endpoints: Adaptive Traffic Profiles & Launch Acceptance Checklist
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Summary: This PRD defines adaptive lane-shaping (per-lane traffic profiles + dynamic weighting) for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: enable product teams to specify lightweight QoS profiles at endpoint-level and route traffic across model variants and capacity tiers while preserving behavioral contracts and SLOs.

Problem statement: Customers using hosted inference are sensitive to tail latency and cost; they also need predictable behavior during capacity pressure. Today we lack fine-grained traffic controls that can: 1) route low-cost/backfill requests to lower-tier capacity, 2) favor high-quality model variants for premium lanes, and 3) gracefully degrade with deterministic behavioral guarantees.

Goals:
- Provide a lane-shaping API/config that accepts: lane policy (priority, cost-bound, deterministic), target SLOs, model preferences, and fallback order.
- Ensure per-lane observable SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, accuracy/regression metrics for eval prompts).
- Implement canary and cutover tools for launch: staged rollout by customer segment and region, with automated halt/rollback triggers.
- Support all hosted surfaces: chat (stateful), completions (stateless), embeddings (batch/sync), rerank (multi-candidate) with lane-aware batching and KV-cache hints.

Non-goals / out of scope:
- Full Dedicated or Private control-plane integration (V1 focuses on hosted).
- New model training or retraining work.
- Cross-customer multi-tenant isolation beyond existing hosted guarantees.

Key constraints:
- Must not increase P99 latency for premium lanes by >10% at launch under nominal traffic.
- Configs are limited to 5 active lanes per endpoint for V1.

Success metrics (launch targets):
- Ability to route >= 90% of traf fic for an endpoint according to configured lane weights within 2 minutes of policy change.
- Premium lane P99 latency within 10% of baseline for each supported surface.
- No customer-visible behavioral regressions for a 500-sample eval suite (per-endpoint) with failure rate < 0.5%.

Telemetry & observability:
- Per-lane dashboards (latency histograms, cost-per-token, model-version split, error rates).
- Alerting: lane_slo_breach (p99 > threshold for 5m), lane_model_fallback_rate (>5% fallback over 10m), lane_regression_alert (eval-set drift).

Compatibility notes for surfaces:
- Chat: preserve KV cache affinity for premium lanes; lane transitions must respect session affinity.
- Completions: support lane preference and batching hints to reduce cost.
- Embeddings: lane-aware batching and regional placement to respect latency SLOs.
- Rerank: ensure multi-candidate scoring runs on the same lane to avoid cross-lane inconsistency.

Documentation: Confluence draft (link in files).
acceptance_criteria: API: Create/update/delete lane-shaping config via hosted endpoint API with validation errors surfaced (400) for invalid policies
Routing: Traffic distribution matches configured weights within +/-5% after a 2-minute stabilization window under steady load
SLOs: For each lane, p50/p95/p99 latency metrics reported; premium lanes p99 increase <=10% vs baseline under normal traffic
Behavioral: Eval suite (500 prompts per endpoint type) runs in staging with <0.5% regression rate and documented test run attached
Affinity: Chat sessions retain lane affinity across retries and short-lived failovers; no session mixups observed in canary tests
Fallbacks: Automatic fallback to compatible model variants triggers and logs when capacity constraints exceed thresholds; fallback rate <5% in steady state
Observability: Per-lane dashboard tiles available in Console and links documented; alerts fire in simulated SLO breach scenarios
Rollout: Canary rollout supports slice control (by account, region) and automated halt/rollback when alert thresholds are crossed
Docs/Guides: Public API docs, quickstart example for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank, and an operational runbook for on-call teams published
Security: Config persisted in customer tenancy with access control; audit log entries recorded on config changes
notes:
Decisions & trade-offs: We prioritize behavioral determinism for premium lanes over absolute cost savings. For V1 we limit lanes to 5 to reduce config complexity.

Open questions: Should per-request hints for lane preference be exposed in SDKs or only via endpoint config? (Action: PM to prototype SDK hint in Cycle 11)

Follow-ups: ENG to provide kernel-level scheduling telemetry (ENG-37100); SRE run synthetic SLO breach tests across regions.

Timeline: Feature branch cut 2026-03-12, internal canary starts 2026-03-18, broad launch target 2026-03-31.

Links and artifacts: See files for Confluence spec, example policies, and PR checklist.
